text:
maria: quick heads-up — I flipped on proxy-protocol on the inference NLB via Terraform to preserve client IPs, and after that we started seeing intermittent 502s for gRPC routes when TLS passthrough is enabled. anyone seen conntrack/timeouts bite like this?

alex: hmm — did you also change externalTrafficPolicy? if it’s Cluster, we can get SNAT + conntrack churn. ExternalTrafficPolicy: Local helps preserve source IP without proxy-proto in some cases.

maria: no change to externalTrafficPolicy, still Cluster. TF change was just adding the annotation: 
```yaml
service.beta.kubernetes.io/aws-load-balancer-proxy-protocol: '*',
service.beta.kubernetes.io/aws-load-balancer-type: "nlb"
```
and gateway is set for TLS passthrough for port 443.

sam: proxy-protocol with TLS passthrough + NLB + kube-proxy iptables sometimes causes conntrack entries to show up as ESTABLISHED but then get reclaimed early if netfilter conntrack_max is low. Also note AWS NLB with proxy protocol injects header and node must decode it — our envoy/nginx listeners need to be proxy-proxy-aware.

jess: are the 502s on the LB or on the backend pods? any 5xx logs from envoy in the pods?

maria: LB 502s mostly. Pod envoy logs show connections reset occasionally. No clear HTTP 5xx from app.

alex: a few quick checks: 1) check conntrack table on nodes (sudo conntrack -L | grep <pod-ip>) 2) check kube-proxy mode (iptables vs ipvs) 3) ensure node listeners (envoy) have `proxy_protocol` enabled if NLB is in proxy-proto mode. If envoy is not expecting it, TLS bytes will look wrong and connections can fail.

maria: good point — envoy config does NOT have proxy_protocol enabled. I thought proxy-protocol annotation was only for forwarding client IP, didn't realize we need to surface it to envoy.

sam: yeah for TLS passthrough we avoid terminating at the LB so proxy-proto is how NLB passes original client IP. If the TCP terminator (envoy) isn't set, you'll get garbled TLS handshake and 502.

jess: two possible mitigation paths: 1) enable `proxy_protocol` on envoy listeners and keep annotation, or 2) remove proxy-protocol and set `externalTrafficPolicy: Local` + preserve source IP via nodeport routing, or 3) switch to ALB with TLS termination (if you can terminate).

maria: we can't terminate TLS at ALB for this tenant (mTLS needs end-to-end). Option 2 sounds less risky for now. Any terraform snippet for externalTrafficPolicy change + healthcheck?

alex: in k8s svc manifest set: 
```yaml
spec:
  type: LoadBalancer
  externalTrafficPolicy: Local
  healthCheckNodePort: 32080  # explicit port so NLB HC uses pod directly
  ports:
    - port: 443
      targetPort: 8443
```
Also remove proxy-protocol annotation. That avoids proxy header but preserves client ip at the node.

sam: and ensure you have a DaemonSet or nodePort open on all nodes, otherwise Local will only send traffic to nodes with endpoints. Also healthCheckNodePort needs to be allowed in security groups.

maria: noted. Another wrinkle — we use Gateway API with SecretBinding in namespace infra-inference. Do we need to rebind secrets if we change from proxy-proto to externalTrafficPolicy?

jess: secretbinding unaffected; that's for TLS certs. TLS passthrough still uses same secret for the gateway route. No secret change needed.

infra-bot: deploy-checklist: - verify envoy proxy_protocol flag in config repo - update svc externalTrafficPolicy in tf (staging first) - ensure healthCheckNodePort is in sg whitelist - run canary in staging

maria: I'll open a TF PR to revert the proxy-protocol annotation and add externalTrafficPolicy: Local + explicit healthCheckNodePort and run in staging. tagging @alex for review.

alex: SG — also add a note to increase conntrack max on nodes temporarily if staging still sees churn: `sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=262144` and monitor `conntrack -S`.

sam: +1. Also check kube-proxy mode — ipvs is friendlier for long-lived gRPC.

maria: thanks all. I'll roll the TF revert now and post results. If we still see 502s after enabling externalTrafficPolicy, we'll try enabling proxy_protocol in envoy instead and run a canary with that config. :thumbsup:

alex: thanks — LMK if you want help with envoy flags or a quick runbook for the change.

maria: will do — PR coming in ~10m.
